item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABNT20 KNHC 291123
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 AM EDT Tue Sep 29 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Fay, located well to the west-southwest of the Azores, and on
Tropical Storm Hanna, located well to the east-northeast of
Bermuda.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected over the next 7 days.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Hanna are issued under WMO
header WTNT33 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPAT3.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Hanna are issued under WMO
header WTNT23 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMAT3.

$$
Forecaster Kelly

MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1010 MB...29.83 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 AM AST (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression Fay was
located near latitude 24.2 North, longitude 47.3 West. The
depression is moving toward the southwest near 12 mph (19 km/h), and
this motion is expected to continue the next couple of days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
Little change in strength is forecast, and Fay is forecast to 
become a post-tropical cyclone on Wednesday.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1010 mb (29.83 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.

-------------

item.title: Tropical Depression Fay Forecast Discussion Number 38
item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM AST Tue Sep 29 2026 
000
WTNT41 KNHC 291449
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Depression Fay Discussion Number  38
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
1100 AM AST Tue Sep 29 2026
 
Fay remains a sheared tropical cyclone, with the low-level center 
completely exposed and all the deep convection sheared well to the 
southwest. This remaining convection continues to be displaced 
further and further away from the low-level center. Recent satellite 
intensity estimates from UW-CIMSS and TAFB have trended downward to 
around 30 kt. Based on these data, the initial intensity for this 
advisory is lowered to 30 kt, making Fay a tropical depression once 
again.

Fay is moving southwestward, or 225/10 kt, steered by a mid-level 
ridge located over the central Atlantic. This general motion is 
expected to continue throughout the remainder of the forecast 
period. The latest NHC track forecast is essentially an update to 
the previous advisory and remains in good agreement with HCCA 
corrected-consensus aid.

The depression is expected to continue to deal with increasing 
vertical wind shear, which should limit convection near the 
low-level center. As Fay moves into a more stable airmass, global 
models are in good agreement that the cyclone will become completely 
devoid of deep convection by Wednesday. The latest NHC intensity 
forecast shows the system becoming a post-tropical remnant low at 
that time, before opening into a trough shortly thereafter. Given 
the increasingly hostile environment, it is entirely possible that 
the system could become post-tropical or dissipate even earlier than 
currently forecast.

MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1004 MB...29.65 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 AM AST (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Hanna was
located near latitude 34.6 North, longitude 45.5 West. Hanna is
moving toward the southeast near 12 mph (19 km/h) and and this
motion is forecast to continue over the next day or so followed by
a turn to the east-northeast.
 
Recent satellite wind data indicates that maximum sustained winds 
are near 40 mph (65 km/h) with higher gusts. Gradual weakening is 
expected during the next couple of days, and Hanna is likely to 
become a post-tropical cyclone by the latter part of this week.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 70 miles (110 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1004 mb (29.65 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------

$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Tropical Storm Hanna Forecast Discussion Number 5
item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM AST Tue Sep 29 2026 
000
WTNT43 KNHC 291449
TCDAT3
 
Tropical Storm Hanna Discussion Number   5
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL082026
1100 AM AST Tue Sep 29 2026
 
Satellite imagery this morning shows that Hanna continues as a 
sheared tropical cyclone with the low-level center mostly exposed to 
the west of the main convective area.  The cyclone also remains just 
south of a weak frontal boundary.  Based on a just received ASCAT 
overpass, the initial intensity is reduced to 35 kt. The 
scatterometer data also suggests that the circulation is becoming 
less well defined as it interacts with the frontal boundary.
 
The initial motion is now 125/10 kt.  There is little change to the 
track forecast reasoning from the previous advisory.  Hanna is 
embedded in the flow between a broad mid-latitude trough to its 
northeast and a larger subtropical ridge to its south. This synoptic 
pattern should result in a southeastward or east-southward motion 
over the next 12-24 h with a gradual decrease in forward speed. An 
east-northeastward motion is then expected as the cyclone becomes 
vertically shallow and influenced by a low-level ridge centered 
south of the Azores.  The new forecast track is similar to the 
previous track and is in best agreement with the HFIP Corrected 
Consensus model.

Hanna should gradually weaken due to shear and dry air entrainment, 
and the system is likely to stop producing convection and 
degenerate to a remnant low between 36-48 h based on global model 
simulated satellite imagery. The system is expected to weaken to a 
trough by 96 h.
